analysis.one_liner: Canara Bank is a large government-owned (public sector) bank offering deposits, loans and retail/corporate/agri banking across India.
analysis.whats_happening: Canara Bank reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of about ₹5,175 crore for the September 2026 quarter (up roughly 8% year-on-year), with net interest income up about 20% and bad loans continuing to fall. Despite this, the stock closed at ₹118.29 on 16 October 2026, essentially at its 52-week low, having fallen about 23% from its February 2026 peak. The board has also approved raising up to $2 billion overseas via bonds, and the next results (December quarter) are expected mid-February 2027 - more than three months away.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a tricky one: the bank's own numbers have been getting better every quarter - profit higher, bad loans fewer, lending growing - but the share price has been sliding and is now at a one-year low. That gap is the central tension here. Part of the explanation is cheap starting valuation and a chronic market discount applied to government-owned banks, but part of it may be the market pricing in risks this report cannot verify. Note also that Canara Bank did a 5-for-1 stock split in May 2024, so today's ₹118 price is not comparable to pre-2024 prices without adjustment - the return figures below already account for this.
analysis.quarters: Profit growth has been consistent and improving: Q4 FY26 (Mar-26) PAT was about ₹4,500-4,574 crore (sources vary slightly, down about 10% YoY on a high base), Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) PAT rose to ₹4,856 crore (+2.2% YoY), and Q2 FY27 (Sep-26) PAT hit a record ₹5,170-5,175 crore (+7.7% to +8.4% YoY depending on source). Net interest income accelerated through the year: ₹9,808 crore (Q4 FY26) to ₹10,215 crore (Q1 FY27, +13.9% YoY) to ₹11,005 crore (Q2 FY27, +20.4% YoY). Gross NPA fell steadily from 1.84% (Mar-26) to 1.57% (Jun-26) to 1.33% (Sep-26); net NPA fell from 0.43% to 0.30% over the same period. On the Q1 FY27 earnings call, management said credit growth of 14.4% YoY was beating its own 10-11% guidance and that it did not expect margin (NIM) to contract, reiterating a 2.50-2.60% NIM band. By the Q2 FY27 call, management reported ROA of 1.04% (within its 1.01-1.05% guidance) and ROE of 18.49%, both ahead of internal targets.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock (split-adjusted) is up about 251%, well ahead of the Nifty's 25%, but behind peer Union Bank's 318%. Over 3 years it is up 72% versus Nifty's 17% but again trails Union Bank's 78%. Over the last 1 year the stock is down 4.1% - milder than the Nifty's 9.5% fall, but Union Bank gained 27.3% in the same period, a wide gap against the closest comparable peer that is worth sitting with. The stock is currently at its 52-week low (₹117.12) and down 23.1% from its February 2026 peak of ₹153.85; this drawdown is a genuine price decline, not a corporate-action artifact - the May 2024 5:1 split is a cosmetic reclassification of share count, not value, and has already been reflected in the return series above.
analysis.valuation_read: Canara Bank trades cheap on headline multiples: P/E is reported between roughly 5.2x and 6.3x depending on the data source and calculation window, and P/B is around 0.87-0.99x, meaning the market values it below its own book of assets. It is cheap for structural reasons common to PSU banks - government ownership overhang, periodic equity dilution through past or planned capital raises, a leaner fee-income mix than private peers, and historically lower return ratios. Whether it is cheap in the sense of mispriced is a separate question: with ROE now reported in the 16-18.5% range (sources disagree, so treat the band rather than a single number) and asset quality improving, a sub-1x book multiple is not obviously justified by current fundamentals - but the 1-year underperformance against Union Bank suggests the market may be discounting something this report could not independently verify. Not verified - check exact TTM P/E and ROE on Screener before relying on a precise figure.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is both volume-led and margin-stable, which is the more durable combination. Net interest income grew 20.4% YoY in the September 2026 quarter on the back of credit growth management described as outperforming its own 14-18% guidance, while NIM held within its stated 2.50-2.60% band rather than being propped up by one-off repricing. Retail/agri/MSME lending reportedly grew faster than the overall book (around 21% YoY as of Q1 FY27), suggesting the growth is not concentrated in a single low-margin corporate segment.
analysis.health_read: Asset quality is the clearer story here: gross NPA nearly halved over three quarters, from 1.84% in March 2026 to 1.33% in September 2026, with net NPA down to 0.30%, implying strong provisioning coverage. Capital adequacy is comfortable at 17.19% CRAR (CET1 around 12.9%), well above regulatory minimums. For a bank, 'profits turning into cash' is better read through falling NPAs and controlled credit cost (reported at 0.47%, below the 0.5% ceiling management targets) than through a conventional cash-flow statement, which was not available to check here. On this basis, business risk (credit quality) looks like it is easing rather than building, and financial risk (capital strength) looks adequately managed, including via the planned $2 billion overseas bond raise, which is debt-funded growth capital rather than a sign of distress.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the Government of India, holding about 62.93% - pledging is not applicable to a government promoter, so there is no pledge risk to flag here. Institutional ownership is modest: FIIs hold about 5.26% and domestic institutions (including mutual funds at ~7%) about 12.38%, with the remainder in public hands. No famous individual investor was found on the shareholding register - if you were expecting to see one, it is not there.
strengths: Gross NPA fell from 1.84% (Mar-26) to 1.33% (Sep-26), with net NPA down to 0.30%, over just two quarters
Q2 FY27 net profit of about ₹5,175 crore was the bank's highest-ever quarterly profit, up roughly 8% YoY
Net interest income growth accelerated to 20.4% YoY in Q2 FY27 alongside credit growth management says is beating its own guidance
Capital adequacy comfortable at 17.19% CRAR with CET1 around 12.9%, well above regulatory minimums
watchpoints: Stock is at a 52-week low (₹117.12) and down 23.1% from its February 2026 peak, even as reported profit and asset quality have been improving - that divergence is unresolved
1-year return of -4.1% lags peer Union Bank's +27.3% by a wide margin, despite Canara Bank's own numbers improving

Valuation ratios vary meaningfully by source: P/E quoted anywhere from about 5.2x to 6.3x and ROE from about 16% to 18.5% depending on the calculation window - verify the precise figure before relying on it
Board has approved raising up to $2 billion overseas via bonds; scale and cost of this funding was not independently verified here
analysis.one_thing: Whether the December 2026 quarter (due mid-February 2027) shows NIM still holding in the 2.50-2.60% band and gross NPA continuing to fall below 1.33% - that would clarify whether the stock's underperformance against Union Bank and its own fundamentals is a market overreaction or reflects a risk not yet visible in the reported numbers.
analysis.data_notes: Core P&L, NII, NPA and CRAR figures were cross-checked across multiple independent outlets (Business Standard, Angel One, PSU Connect, Kotak Neo, Indian Mastermind, Kalkine, EquityBulls) and the bank's own earnings-call commentary, and are consistent to within rounding. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE) showed real disagreement across sources (e.g. P/E 5.26 vs 5.94 vs ~6.3; ROE 16.1% vs 16.77% vs 17.99% vs 18.49%) depending on TTM window and whether the figure is quarterly-annualized - these were reported as ranges rather than averaged. A reported subsidiary stake-sale item (Canara HSBC Life, Canara Robeco) turned out to be dated 2025, not within the July-October 2026 window, and was excluded. Operating cash-flow detail was not independently verified; asset-quality trend was used as the health proxy instead, which is standard for banks.
